mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate below 5% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE < 5% for two consecutive months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals supply-side weakness, which raises input costs and reduces output, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of persistent industrial production contraction (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise of at least 0.4 percentage points in UNRATE and a fall of at least 1% in PAYEMS within the same month signals a sharp deterioration in labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.4pp AND PAYEMS falls > 1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both UNRATE rises > 0.4pp and PAYEMS falls > 1% in the same month (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in both HOUST and RSAFS for three consecutive months signals a drop in housing and retail demand, which negatively impacts construction and consumer discretionary sectors, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both decline for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both HOUST and RSAFS decline for three consecutive months (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month drop in FEDFUNDS below 1% during a period of low inflation (CPIAUCSL < 2% annualized) signals an accommodative monetary policy in a low-rate environment, which supports risk assets and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS drops > 0.75pp in one month AND CPIAUCSL < 2% annualized
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS drops sharply and inflation is low (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized GDP growth (GDPC1) above 4% for three consecutive quarters signals a strong demand environment, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when GDPC1 exceeds 4% annualized for three consecutive quarters (t-test p > 0.05).
